title: Duyfken Landfall in Australia
summary: In 1606 the Dutch East India Company ship Duyfken, captained by Willem Janszoon, reached the western coast of Cape York Peninsula, making landfall at the Pennefather River. It is the earliest recorded European contact with the Australian continent. The crew mapped part of the coast, and about nine died in a clash with Wik people.

uncertainty.note: Sources give timing loosely: late February and early March 1606 (National Museum of Australia), probably early 1606 (WA Museum). Exact-day claims on other web pages conflict and are not used.

where.modern_name: Pennefather River, western Cape York Peninsula, Queensland, Australia (pin is the gazetteer point for the river, a proxy for the landfall)
where.historical_name: Western coast of Cape York Peninsula (no contemporary name given in sources)

importance.justification: Earliest recorded European contact with the Australian continent, and the first mapping of part of its coast.

audience_note: Involves a violent clash in which about nine crew members died; sources differ on how it arose.

sources.title: Great Southern Land: The maritime exploration of Terra Australis
sources.publisher: Australian Government, Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

sources.title: Pennefather River (Place Names of Australia, from Geoscience Australia)
